\subsection{Suite summary: accuracy losses first}
\label{sec:results-summary}

Table~\ref{tab:N1-main}: suite means with bootstrap 95\% CIs; paired
deltas, tests, and Bonferroni family ($13$ tests, adjusted
$\alpha \approx 0.0038$) from \texttt{stats.json}. Three of 13
survive correction: RULER SemPointer-vs-full, RULER
SemPointer-vs-BM25, LongBench SemPointer-vs-full [ESTABLISHED].

RULER containment ($n=180$ pairs): SemPointer $0.3300$
vs $0.7000$ full, delta $-0.37$,
95\% CI $[-0.44,-0.30]$, McNemar $b=1$, $c=61$,
$p \approx 6.7\times10^{-14}$, surviving Bonferroni [ESTABLISHED]. Vs
BM25 ($0.5778$) delta $-0.248$, CI $[-0.314,-0.183]$,
$p \approx 2.3\times10^{-10}$, likewise surviving [ESTABLISHED]. Vs
dense RAG ($0.3289$) the pointer contributes nothing: delta
$+0.0011$, CI $[-0.003,+0.006]$, zero discordants
($b=c=0$, $p=1.0$; Wilcoxon $p=0.65$) [ESTABLISHED]. RAG/SemPointer
rows match across the taxonomy
(Table~\ref{tab:N5-taxonomy}: both hit~57, miss~123, retrieval-miss~51)
[ESTABLISHED].

LongBench F1: SemPointer ($0.0773$, $n=1150$) trails full
($0.1112$, $n=1136$ scored) by $-0.033$, CI
$[-0.040,-0.027]$ over $n=1136$ matched pairs, Wilcoxon
$p \approx 1.6\times10^{-31}$, surviving Bonferroni [ESTABLISHED].
SemPointer-vs-RAG $-0.0009$, CI $[-0.0047,+0.0028]$, $p=0.32$;
SemPointer-vs-BM25 $-0.0040$, CI $[-0.010,+0.002]$, $p=0.156$: neither
significant [ESTABLISHED]. Figure~\ref{fig:N1-pareto} plots the
trade-offs.

LoCoMo token-F1 ($n=199$ pairs): SemPointer
($0.0518$) trails full ($0.0642$) by $-0.012$, CI
$[-0.022,-0.003]$, Wilcoxon $p=0.028$ --- nominally positive but
\textit{not} significant after Bonferroni; no difference claimed
[ESTABLISHED]. SemPointer-vs-RAG ($+0.0017$, CI $[-0.005,+0.008]$,
$p=0.69$), SemPointer-vs-BM25 ($-0.011$, CI $[-0.022,+0.001]$,
$p=0.037$): neither significant after correction [ESTABLISHED].
No superiority over BM25/full on any suite claimed
[REASONED].

\subsection{RULER per-task: easy parity, hard collapse}
\label{sec:results-ruler}

Table~\ref{tab:N2-ruler-pertask} and Figure~\ref{fig:N2-ruler} split RULER
into $n=30$ cells. Easiest needle
\texttt{niah\_single\_1}: SemPointer matches full
($0.9667 = 0.9667$) [ESTABLISHED]. Harder cells separate:
\texttt{niah\_single\_2} $0.2000$ vs $1.0000$ full,
\texttt{niah\_single\_3} $0.2667$ vs $0.7000$,
\texttt{multikey\_1} $0.4667$ vs $0.9333$ [ESTABLISHED]. Variable
tracking / common-word extraction collapse
all sparse systems: SemPointer $0.0733$ on vt vs
$0.5933$ full; cwe floored at $0.0067$ in all
four including full: task bound, not retrieval effect [ESTABLISHED]. BM25 beats SemPointer on harder NIAH
($0.8000$ and $0.6667$ on \texttt{single\_2}/\texttt{single\_3}),
consistent with lexical needles failing under dense cosine at $m=1$ [REASONED].

\subsection{Efficiency: large token and latency reductions at lower accuracy}
\label{sec:results-efficiency}

Table~\ref{tab:N3-efficiency} and Figure~\ref{fig:N3-efficiency} give
active tokens, latency, peak VRAM with sparse/full
ratios. SemPointer uses $\sim$one-tenth active context:
$1270.3$ vs $13089.2$ tokens on RULER (ratio $0.097$),
$963.5$ vs $13066.1$ on LongBench ($0.074$), $987.3$ vs $14525.1$ on
LoCoMo ($0.068$) --- $10$--$15\times$ fewer [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{metrics.json}).
Latency: $894.5$ vs $7256.9$~ms RULER
($0.123$, $\sim$$8\times$), $1527.2$ vs $8084.5$~ms LongBench ($0.189$,
$\sim$$5\times$), $1308.8$ vs $5326.2$~ms LoCoMo ($0.246$, $\sim$$4\times$)
[ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{metrics.json}). Peak VRAM $3463.0$ to $2331.2$~MB RULER
($0.673$), $2994.4$ to $2300.5$~MB LongBench ($0.768$), $3825.1$ to
$2302.6$~MB LoCoMo ($0.602$) [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{metrics.json}). Per
\S\ref{sec:results-summary} savings accompany losses without offset; no net-benefit claim [REASONED]. Pointer costs over RAG: $+363$
active tokens/request on RULER ($1270.3$ vs $907.2$), $\sim$$+395$ on
LongBench, $+416$ on LoCoMo, for RULER delta $+0.001$
[ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{metrics.json}).

\subsection{Failure taxonomy}
\label{sec:results-taxonomy}

Table~\ref{tab:N5-taxonomy} classifies scored misses from
\texttt{error\_breakdown.json} (miss := score $< 1.0$ containment or
$< 0.5$ F1; retrieval-miss := miss with no selected block overlapping gold) [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{error\_breakdown.json}). The thresholds follow the scoring scales: containment is binary so any $<1.0$ is a miss, while $0.5$ F1 requires at least half token overlap, separating retrieval/generation failure from partial-credit noise [REASONED].
RULER: SemPointer's 123 misses split 51 retrieval-miss / 66
block-hit-wrong (gold selected, answer wrong) / 6
gold-not-localizable (unlocalizable under production chunking) [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{error\_breakdown.json}).
Per \S\ref{sec:results-summary}, dense RAG shares it (51/66/6):
selection, not pointer encoding, binds [REASONED]. LongBench:
retrieval-miss (465), block-hit-wrong (253); 409 of
1150 gold-not-localizable: over a third rewards no
block selection under 512-token chunking, compressing all
headroom [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{error\_breakdown.json}). LoCoMo: 157 of 199
gold-not-localizable for SemPointer (157 full too); 28 retrieval-miss,
14 block-hit-wrong; hits 0 of 199
[ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{error\_breakdown.json}). Two modes recur [REASONED]: boundary splits
(gold straddling a 512-token edge, no block contains it), multihop splits
(two hotpotqa/2wikimqa or two-to-four musique facts in
different blocks; $m=1$ resolves one). Per-task tables substitute
since items lack hop labels (\texttt{error\_breakdown.json}: hotpotqa/2wikimqa
2-hop by construction, musique 2--4-hop) [ESTABLISHED].

\subsection{Missing-data disclosure}
\label{sec:results-oom}

LongBench full: $n=1136$ of 1150 scored; 14 narrativeqa
full-context OOMs on the 8\,GB card excluded
[ESTABLISHED]. Missingness hits longest narrativeqa contexts, so scored-only
full ($0.1112$) drops hardest full cases, favoring
full; errors-as-zero full $0.1099$; SemPointer on
those 14 OOM identifiers $0.0343$ --- sparse answered
cases full could not attempt [ESTABLISHED]
(\texttt{stats.json}: \texttt{oom\_sensitivity}). Both reported;
paired delta (see \S\ref{sec:results-summary}) uses matched scored rows only [ESTABLISHED].
RULER: 10 full-context OOM rows superseded by scored retries
after resume, excluded throughout; zero truly missing
rows [ESTABLISHED]. Retry latency for these 10 RULER retries is excluded with no cost accounting, so full-context latency is understated and the gap remains unmeasured [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{stats.json}: \texttt{oom\_sensitivity}).

\subsection{Multi-hop pilot: nine arms, two clean negatives}
\label{sec:results-pilot}

Table~\ref{tab:N6-pilot} covers four pilots on the same 30 musique
examples (2--4-hop), identical model/seed/config: nine arms
matched-pair comparable; CIs overlap, no
significance claimed [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{metrics.json}, \texttt{config\_table.json}). SemPointer point-estimates first
($0.0541$ vs $0.0468$ full, $0.0313$ RAG, $0.0245$ BM25) at $16\times$ fewer
tokens than full ($1059$ vs $16925$) [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{metrics.json}). Two mechanism tests
negative. First, LLM routing from pointer index fails twice:
\texttt{agentic\_pointer} ($0.0299$ at $3285$ tokens) and redesigned
\texttt{agentic\_pointer\_v2} with keyword-enriched index and constrained
multi-block grammar ($0.0233$ at $3863$ tokens) both trail dense top-$1$
($0.0541$ at $1059$ tokens); v2 routes one block on 30/30:
model-scale capacity, not prompt design; single-model $n{=}30$
cannot establish structurality; no v3 [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{metrics.json}). Second,
discrete-address retrieval
(\texttt{address\_rag}, pointer-ID overlap only): $0.0268$
at $581$ tokens, $\sim$86\% of dense RAG's $0.0313$ --- pointer IDs carry
signal (k load-bearing per CPU tests), no gain over dense cosine [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{metrics.json}).
Two-round retrieval
($0.0283$ at $1323$ tokens) matches single-round RAG; hybrid fusion
($0.0216$) at BM25/RAG floor [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{metrics.json}).
\texttt{session\_summary} excluded: per-chunk loop
records $10$--$17$k active tokens/request, exceeding full --- token-accounting
defect under repair, not a result [ESTABLISHED].
